**Keywords:** Replace with 3-5 terms relevant to your application and methods.

**Template note (remove before submission).** Write **8-10 pages of main text**, counting the abstract, Sections 1-6, and their figures, tables, captions, equations, and code examples. Exclude a separate title-only cover page, References, Author contributions, and appendices or supplementary material. The first page here includes the abstract and counts as a main-text page. References starts on a new page to mark the end of the counted text. This short template illustrates structure, not the required report length.

# Introduction

State the substantive question and why it matters. Distinguish the question about adjusted association from the question about predicting new outcomes. Cite relevant background and preview the report's contribution.

# Data and study design

Describe the original data source, observational unit, response units, candidate predictors, collection process, sample size, exclusions, and missing-value handling. Explain dependence or grouping if present.

Include a motivating plot based on the training data, with units, legend, and a caption. Explain the train/test split and how it respects the study design. Keep the test outcomes out of exploration and model selection.

# Linear regression analysis

Write and explain the model, assumptions, coding, and any transformations or interactions. Interpret at least two meaningful coefficients or contrasts with estimates and 95% confidence intervals.

Compare one scientifically motivated reduced/full model pair using the same training observations and response scale. State the restriction, test, and limitations. Include residual-versus-fitted, normal Q-Q, and influence assessments; explain any action taken. Acknowledge exploratory model selection and distinguish association from causation.

# Machine learning method

Describe one regression algorithm and why it fits the prediction task. State the available predictors, training-based preprocessing, tuning settings, and validation design. Keep learned preprocessing inside each training fold and finalize both models before examining test performance.

# Results and predictive comparison

Compare the training-mean baseline, final linear regression, and chosen machine learning method on the same test observations. Report test RMSE and MAE in original response units and explain any inverse response transformation.

| Model | Test RMSE | Test MAE |
|:---|---:|---:|
| Training-mean baseline | Replace | Replace |
| Multiple linear regression | Replace | Replace |
| Chosen machine learning method | Replace | Replace |

Add observed-versus-predicted plots for both fitted models, interpret errors, and explain whether the difference matters in this application. Generate all reported numbers and figures from the submitted source.

# Discussion and conclusion

Answer the research question. Explain substantive findings, uncertainty, practical model choice, and limits to generalization. Discuss at least one limitation and one useful next step.

# References {.unnumbered}

Replace this prompt with complete author-year references for data, methods, software, and adapted code. If using a BibTeX file, add `bibliography: references.bib` to the YAML and cite entries in the text. Include the bibliography file with your submission.

# Author contributions {.unnumbered}

List each author's contribution, or state that this is an individual project.

# Supplementary material {.unnumbered}

Include supporting code and additional output as needed. Record seed 8561, split identifiers, software versions, data-access instructions, and fresh-session rendering steps. All main-text figures and tables should be reproducible from the submitted files.
